subject: Steering committee: Novanta production impact & executive briefing
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novanta.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: support@novanta.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production spike — API latencies, increasing errors (urgent)

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing a significant performance regression in our production integration around 08:45 PT. Latency has climbed from ~1.2s median to ~4.6s and our 5xx error rate has spiked from 0.8% to ~6.3%. Throughput (requests/min) has dropped by roughly 28% compared to the 24h baseline. This is impacting real-time inference in our triage workflow — several clinicians are reporting slow response and some timeouts.

We've attached a short telemetry export and a screenshot from our SLO dashboard showing the timeline. Can you triage and confirm whether this is on Redwood's side? This is customer-impacting for us. We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you plan any fallback or traffic routing (we have a multi-region failover but would prefer guidance).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability
Novanta Medical

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novanta.com>, support@novanta.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike — API latencies, increasing errors (urgent)

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the export. We see the same regression in our edge telemetry. Immediate notes:
- Median latency up from ~1.1s to ~4.5s across the eu/us clusters starting 08:40 PT.
- Error spike correlates with a higher proportion of tokenization failures and OOM retriable 5xx from the inference runtime on a subset of model variants.
- Autoscaler logs show a handful of allocation timeouts in one Dedicated pool during the window.

I'm assembling a small steering committee to coordinate a focused response (ops + infra + customer liaison). Preliminary plan: (1) route Novanta traffic to a stable variant in us-west-2 that bypasses the latest quantized runtime, (2) attach an emergency burst node pool to absorb queued requests, (3) open a targeted rollback of the recent kernel selection change in the affected pool if routing doesn't stabilize within 30 minutes.

I'll keep cadence updates every 30 minutes until resolved. Can you confirm whether Novanta can accept the temporary model-variant routing we propose? Also tagging Laurel in case legal needs to be aware of any interim SLA credits.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Steering committee — initial triage & action items

Team — quick findings from infra and runtime:
- Root-cause hypothesis: a recent kernel-selection heuristic (deploy 20270606-14:05) is selecting a quantized execution path that interacts poorly with longer-than-expected sequence prefixes Novanta sends, causing KV cache thrash and increased GC/eviction cycles. The thrash is amplifying memory pressure and producing retriable 5xx.
- Evidence: allocation/eviction spike aligned with the latency window in the dedicated pool; the us-west-2 stable variant (older kernel) shows no such pattern.
- Immediate actions (in order):
  1) Initiate routing policy override: direct 100% Novanta prod traffic to the us-west-2 stable variant (Grace will run).
  2) Spin a small burst pool and temporarily lift per-request CPU guardrails for Novanta (Ben will coordinate).
  3) Hold rollback of kernel heuristic for monitored 60 minutes if routing doesn't bring errors under 1%.

I'll update telemetry after the routing change. If we confirm improvement, we'll draft a short postmortem and recommend a conservative kernel-selection rollback + additional canary checks before re-enabling the heuristic.

Marissa
Sr. Infrastructure PM
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: ceo@redwood.com, cto@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Briefing: Novanta impact — executive summary & asks (for leadership)

Leaders — brief summary and immediate asks so you have one place to see the timeline:
- Impact: Novanta (large Tier-1 healthcare customer) experienced increased latencies (median ~4.5s) and a 5xx error spike to ~6% between 08:40–09:10 PT. Customer throughput dropped ~28%. Potential clinical impact reported.
- Likely cause: kernel-selection heuristic from 20270606 deploy causing KV-cache thrash on longer prefixes. Evidence from allocation logs and unaffected stable variant in us-west-2.
- Actions taken: routing override to stable variant executed 09:02 PT; burst pool attached 09:08 PT; observed error rate drop to ~1.1% by 09:25 PT and median latency returning to ~1.4s by 09:30 PT.
- Current status (10:20 PT): customer is stable on the fallback variant; telemetry looks healthy but we have to validate no downstream data-quality regressions from variant differences.

Asks:
1) Approve a conservative rollback of the 20270606 kernel heuristic in prod tomorrow 02:00 PT maintenance window (will require ops runway + QA).
2) Approve up to $12k emergency cloud burst cost for the Dedicated pool for the next 48 hours while we validate the rollback and test canaries.
3) Outreach approval for a joint executive update to Novanta (30-min briefing + written timeline) to be sent today at ~11:00 PT.

I'll run the customer briefing and own communications; Marissa will draft the technical postmortem. If approved, legal should draft the short note on potential SLA implications.

— Jonas

Jonas / team — thanks for the focused response and the walkthrough this morning. The temporary routing reduced errors and latency as you reported; clinicians were able to resume normal workflows by ~09:35 PT.

Two quick asks from Novanta: (1) can Redwood confirm the expected behavioral differences between the stable variant and the quantized variant so we can validate outputs for a sample set of queries, and (2) we would like a short joint summary for our executive leadership by EOD today that states root cause, mitigation steps, and next steps (including rollback timing and expected risk).

We're available for the 11:00 PT briefing. Please include any relevant telemetry snapshots and the suggested postmortem outline.

Best,
Elena

Novanta Medical
